title: Weird behaviour of Root Motion when blending animations.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable, latest master branch as of 2026/01/24.

### System information

Linux - Godot 4.5.1.stable - Vulkan(Forward+)

### Issue description

There seems to be an issue with the way root motion position is being calculated when blending between animations.
Sometimes it just zips forwards by a lot. It kind of reminds me of that Elden Ring bug that made it so if you pressed slightly forward eventually you'd just go flying forward a long distance, but not as exaggerated of course.
I'm not sure what could be causing it, it could be that the animation is looping and somehow that messes up the length of the root motion, or I don't know.

I tried looking through the animation mixer code for the blending and found that in fact sometimes "loc[1]" becomes very large compared to "loc[0]" (like, [X, Y, 2.8] vs [X, Y, 0.9] respectively for example), but I could not really dig deeper or understand where all of the values come from as I don't have the time or patience right now to begin understanding all the code behind it.

I'll attach a video down below showing the issue in the provided MRP.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a026e97-63f3-4073-bda2-7df171b6aa5b

I guess it could also be an issue on my end, maybe I set the root motion wrong, maybe my animations are messed up somehow, or the fact that the animations are not the same length is the issue, or simply the way I set up the animation tree.
I've tried looking for how other people set their root motion and stuff and haven't seen anything inherently wrong with how I did it, but who knows.
If that's the case, please let me know and sorry for opening the issue.
Thanks!

EDIT:
I forgot to mention, but even when it doesn't zip forward, for some reason when switching between walking to jogging, jogging to sprinting, or vice versa, the character seems to slow down and then re-accelerate. This becomes clearer if you increase the transition time between animations, maybe to like 5 seconds, and if you do that, you can actually see the animations going crazy while blending every time they loop (or at least I assume it's happening when they loop).

### Steps to reproduce

Download and run the MRP, hold "shift" and spam "W", "A", "S" or "D" for the clearest example.
It also happens if you hold a moving direction and switch between holding and releasing control, although to a lesser degree, since the root motion difference between the walking and jogging animation is lesser than idle and sprinting. Plus, it happens with any animation transition to a bigger or lesser degree.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[root_motion_issue_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24839736/root_motion_issue_mrp.zip)
